tracks.narration: When a circuit has no series or parallel pairs to collapse, sometimes you can convert a triangle of resistors into a star — same terminals, simpler shape.
Three nodes A, B, C with a resistor between every pair — that's a delta. Each branch carries the two-node label R sub A B, R sub B C, R sub C A.
Hold the three corner terminals fixed. Slide the three resistors inward — now they meet at a single point N. Same three nodes, same external behaviour, but Y-shaped.
Each Y spoke equals the product of its two adjacent delta sides divided by the sum of all three. R sub A is the product of the two branches meeting at A — divided by the total.
Now any bridge or mesh that defeated series-parallel reduction is back in play. Convert the awkward triangle and the rest collapses.
